hazard_chain: 1. Multi-day pre-monsoon moisture convergence (Western Disturbance + Monsoon trough)
2. High-intensity orographic cloudburst on pre-saturated upper slopes (>375mm in 24h)
3. Moraine-dammed Chorabari Lake (Gandhi Sarovar) overtopping & breach outburst
4. High-velocity boulder/debris hyper-concentrated flow through Kedarnath township
5. Downstream bridge failure, road washout, and alluvial fan inundation
cause_primary: Extreme Multi-Day Rainfall Combined with Moraine-Dammed Lake Outburst (GLOF)
cause_contributing: Early onset of intense monsoon interacting with late-season Western Disturbance
Rapid snowmelt contributing to saturated catchment baseflow
Debris loading from high-gradient mountain tributaries
Chorabari moraine failure releasing ~0.4 million m³ impounded water in minutes
data_availability_before_event: Coarse-resolution IMD gridded rainfall, low station density in high Himalayas, no real-time telemetry on Chorabari moraine.

key_facts.fact: Official estimated death toll exceeded 5,700 people (NDMA official figures)
key_facts.source: NDMA / Government of Uttarakhand Special Report 2013

key_facts.fact: Rainfall recorded over 375 mm in 24h at Dehradun and over 325 mm in Rudraprayag basin
Chorabari Lake outburst breached at ~07:15 AM IST on 17 June 2013
key_facts.source: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG) Post-Event Survey

evidence_claims.claim: 5,748 individuals officially declared missing and presumed dead across 5 districts.

lessons: Need for micro-watershed antecedent moisture tracking rather than daily aggregated totals
Critical requirement for upstream moraine/glacial lake monitoring sensors
Evacuation lead time must account for narrow valley road choke points and bridge bottlenecks
